component: HTTP/3 (QUIC compatibility layer for OpenSSL before 3.5.1)
classes: Assumptions broken by callbacks and reentrancy
root_cause: With the OpenSSL compatibility layer, the QUIC transport parameters custom TLS extension was registered only in the SSL contexts of virtual servers reachable over QUIC, but the SNI ClientHello callback can replace the SSL context with SSL_set_SSL_CTX() between OpenSSL collecting and parsing extensions, so the number of custom extensions no longer matched the array sized for them and the array overflowed.
notes: Affected 1.29.2-1.31.5; fixed in 1.31.6 and 1.30.5. Reached only with HTTP/3 over the OpenSSL compatibility layer (CHANGES: OpenSSL 3.5.0 and earlier) and SNI selecting a virtual server not reachable over QUIC. The fix commit message says the ClientHello callback came from 0373fe5 (https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/0373fe5d98c1515640e74fa6f4d32fac1f1d3ab2; release-1.29.2 is the oldest tag containing it). The OpenSSL-internal point where the extension array is sized and then parsed is taken from that message, not read in OpenSSL. Follow-up 22ba566 (https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/22ba5662440d2865153ac1ff7de5f2b171414346) makes non-QUIC handshakes ignore the extension instead of failing. For a blind audit also give the reviewer ngx_http_ssl_init() in src/http/modules/ngx_http_ssl_module.c and the ClientHello callback in src/event/ngx_event_openssl.c.

classes: Assumptions broken by callbacks and reentrancy
root_cause: The script engine sizes a string expression in a length pass and fills it in a separate copy pass, but the copy codes did not check the remaining buffer space, so when evaluation between the passes changed a value (a map with regex matching rewriting the captures, or a non-cacheable volatile variable evaluating differently) the copy overran the heap buffer.
notes: Affected 0.9.6-1.31.2; fixed in 1.31.3 and 1.30.4. Fix spans three commits in parent order: b767540 adds an e->end pointer and ngx_http_script_check_length() to every copy code (http and stream), 4d32a27 does the same for access log copy operations, 25f920e for direct script evaluation in proxy, proxy_v2, fastcgi, scgi, uwsgi, grpc, index and try_files. freenginx counterpart of the first commit: https://freenginx.org/hg/nginx/rev/d172f506ab5f. The trigger needs a map with regex matching whose variable follows a capture in the same expression, or a volatile map; for a blind audit also give the reviewer the map module and src/http/ngx_http_variables.c.

root_cause: When ngx_http_regex_exec() reallocated r->captures for a cloned subrequest (the realloc_captures path), it did not reset r->ncaptures, so on a failed match it returned early with the old capture count paired with the new uninitialized array, and later unnamed capture reads used uninitialized offsets.
notes: Affected 1.15.8-1.31.2; fixed in 1.31.3 and 1.30.4. The fix commit says the bug was introduced by 746fba0 (https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/746fba0d79c6909e9e09b4d1cb9ddbf052ab545e), which copies captures to cloned subrequests in ngx_http_subrequest() and sets r->realloc_captures. Reached with unnamed regex captures used together with the slice directive or background cache update.

root_cause: ngx_http_post_request() did not check whether the request was already in the posted requests list, so a subrequest posted once by ngx_http_subrequest() and again by ngx_http_postpone_filter() could be finalized twice, decrementing r->main->count one time too many and freeing the main request while it was still in use.
notes: Affected 0.8.11-1.31.2; fixed in 1.31.3 and 1.30.4. Per the commit message, the double post happens with ngx_http_ssi_filter_module during unbuffered proxying when an SSI include subrequest is created while the main request has data postponed by another include. The fix also resets r->write_event_handler during subrequest finalization as hardening. For a blind audit also give the reviewer ngx_http_subrequest() in src/http/ngx_http_core_module.c, the postpone filter and the SSI filter.

root_cause: ngx_http_v3_get_insert_buffer() allocated the session-level QPACK insert buffer from the pool of the encoder unidirectional stream instead of the connection pool, and ngx_http_v3_register_uni_stream() only rejected a second encoder stream while the first still existed, so after that stream closed (connection close is asynchronous) a new encoder stream could reuse the freed buffer.
notes: Affected 1.31.0-1.31.1; fixed in 1.31.2. Fix spans two commits: ceccdbd moves the allocation to the connection pool; 9e29376 records every standard client unidirectional stream type ever created (created_streams mask) and rejects re-creation. HTTP/3 only. Reported by Trung Nguyen of CyStack; the CyStack write-up named in the record was not located, so only the F5 advisory is listed.

root_cause: ngx_http_grpc_create_request() and ngx_http_proxy_v2_create_request() reserved a fixed 4 bytes for each HPACK string length prefix when sizing the request buffer but did not limit header name and value lengths, so very long fields whose length needs a 5-byte prefix made the writes exceed the computed size.
notes: Affected 1.13.10-1.31.1; fixed in 1.31.2 and 1.30.3. Needs ignore_invalid_headers off and large_client_header_buffers large enough for a field over about 2 MB (CHANGES and winfunc). The fix adds NGX_HTTP_V2_MAX_FIELD checks on method, URI, host and header fields. The same bug is in both modules; the audit scope uses the grpc module, and ngx_http_proxy_v2_module.c can be audited as a second target. 26d824e cites the earlier related fix for HTTP/2 response headers, 58a7bc3 (https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/58a7bc3406ac8b9dc0e0afafc69ba42df56009e3), which is not the fix for this CVE.

root_cause: In ngx_http_charset_recode_from_utf8(), when an invalid byte fell inside a saved partial UTF-8 character, ngx_utf8_decode() stopped advancing at that byte and the input position derived from it was not adjusted to cover the whole saved sequence, so the code stepped back 1 byte before the start of the input buffer.
notes: Affected 0.3.50-1.31.1; fixed in 1.31.2 and 1.30.3. Reached only when decoding from UTF-8 via charset_map. Follow-up to 696a7f1 (CVE-2026-42934) in the same function; the vulnerable_ref already contains that earlier fix.

root_cause: For a rewrite replacement without variables, ngx_http_script_regex_start_code() computed the escaping growth once over the whole matched URI, but the copy escapes each referenced capture separately, so overlapping captures (for example $1$2 over nested groups) were escaped more times than counted and overflowed the heap buffer when the replacement was a redirect or contained arguments.
notes: Affected 0.1.17-1.31.0; fixed in 1.31.1 and 1.30.2. The record also names 475732a (https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/475732a3f9dfe82fc2ecdb0a7426083c9c1ee965), the parent of the fix in the same release; its message says it hardens is_args handling after the CVE-2026-42945 fix, so it is not listed as a fix here. The vulnerable_ref already contains 475732a.

root_cause: ngx_http_proxy_v2_create_request() put a request body set by proxy_set_body into a single HTTP/2 DATA frame without splitting it, so a body above 16M overflowed the 24-bit frame length field and the remaining bytes were sent unframed and parsed by the backend as new frames.
notes: Affected 1.29.4-1.30.0; fixed in 1.31.0 and 1.30.1. Reached only with proxy_set_body when proxying to an HTTP/2 backend. The commit notes the single frame could also exceed the 16K default frame size and the available send window.

root_cause: ngx_http_script_regex_end_code() did not clear e->is_args after a rewrite replacement containing arguments, so captures evaluated later by set or if were URI-escaped in the copy pass (ngx_http_script_copy_capture_code) while ngx_http_script_complex_value_code() had sized the buffer without escaping, overflowing it.
notes: Affected 0.6.27-1.30.0; fixed in 1.31.0 and 1.30.1. Needs a rewrite whose replacement has arguments, followed by set or if using an unnamed capture. Follow-up hardening 475732a (1.31.1, https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/475732a3f9dfe82fc2ecdb0a7426083c9c1ee965) also resets e->is_args at rewrite start and copies it into the length engine (le.is_args) in ngx_http_script_complex_value_code(); the record's wording 'the length sub-engine did not inherit it' matches that follow-up.

root_cause: When the first upstream response line was not recognized as a status line, ngx_http_scgi_process_status_line() and ngx_http_uwsgi_process_status_line() fell back to header parsing without resetting the parser state r->state, and without rewinding to the line start when the line had been split across reads, so header parsing resumed from a stale intermediate state.
notes: Affected 0.8.42-1.30.0; fixed in 1.31.0 and 1.30.1. Fix spans two commits: f79c286 resets r->state before the fallback; 5f86648 adds line_start to ngx_http_status_t so the fallback rewinds a split first line (it also changes the proxy module's HTTP/0.9 fallback). How the stale state leads to the over-read is inferred in the record, not stated in the commits. The uwsgi module has the same code and can be audited as a second target.

root_cause: When a multi-byte UTF-8 character was split across three or more single-byte buffers, ngx_http_charset_recode_from_utf8() passed the last saved-array index instead of the saved byte count to ngx_utf8_decode() and then used that index as the ngx_memcpy() length, reading past the end of the input buffer.
notes: Affected 0.3.50-1.30.0; fixed in 1.31.0 and 1.30.1. Reached only when decoding from UTF-8 via charset_map. CVE-2026-48142 is a later fix in the same function, so the vulnerable_ref contains both bugs.

root_cause: On client address migration, ngx_quic_handle_migration() switched the connection to the new path before path validation completed, so QUIC streams created in the meantime received the unvalidated, possibly spoofed, client address; the fix sets the connection path only after validation succeeds.
notes: Affected 1.25.0-1.30.0; fixed in 1.31.0 and 1.30.1. HTTP/3 (QUIC listeners) only.

root_cause: The OCSP context did not keep the resolver context of its pending OCSP responder name resolution, so when the client connection closed (typically on timeout) ngx_ssl_ocsp_done() freed the OCSP context without cancelling the resolution, and ngx_ssl_ocsp_resolve_handler() later used the freed context.
notes: Affected 1.19.0-1.30.0; fixed in 1.31.0 and 1.30.1. Reached only with ssl_ocsp (client certificate OCSP validation) and a resolver for the responder name.

root_cause: ngx_http_dav_copy_move_handler() mapped the Destination URI to a file path in a location using alias without checking that it was at least as long as the location prefix that alias replaces, so the unsigned length subtraction in ngx_http_map_uri_to_path() underflowed and the path copy overwrote the heap buffer.
notes: Affected 0.5.13-1.29.6; fixed in 1.29.7 and 1.28.3. Needs dav_methods COPY or MOVE in a location with alias. Location matching guarantees the prefix only for the request URI, not for the Destination URI used afterwards. The underflow happens in the http core function ngx_http_map_uri_to_path() (named in the commit message; its file was not read); the fix is in the DAV handler.

root_cause: The mp4 atom readers checked that entries times the entry size fit in the atom using native word arithmetic, so on 32-bit platforms a large entries count overflowed the product and passed the check, letting later processing read and write outside the mp4 buffer.
notes: Affected 1.1.19-1.29.6; fixed in 1.29.7 and 1.28.3. Only 32-bit builds are affected; the fix casts entries to uint64_t in the size checks. Tell the blind auditor the target platform is 32-bit, or the bug is not reachable.

root_cause: Boundary checks in ngx_http_mp4_process() and the stsz, stco and co64 update functions used strict comparisons where non-strict ones were needed (< instead of <=, > instead of >=), so empty ranges and empty stco or co64 atoms were not rejected, leading to out-of-bounds reads and writes.
notes: Affected 1.1.19-1.29.6; fixed in 1.29.7 and 1.28.3. The vulnerable_ref also contains CVE-2026-27784 (fixed in the next commit), so a report may find both.

root_cause: ngx_mail_auth_http_create_request() cleared only s->passwd.data and not its length for the CRAM-MD5 and APOP methods, so on an authentication retry the session held a NULL password pointer with a nonzero length, which was then dereferenced.
notes: Affected 0.5.15-1.29.6; fixed in 1.29.7 and 1.28.3. Needs CRAM-MD5 or APOP with authentication retry enabled. The fix replaces the pointer-only reset with ngx_str_null(&s->passwd).

root_cause: ngx_mail_smtp_resolve_addr_handler() stored the host name from the reverse (PTR) DNS lookup of the client address without checking its characters, and that name was later inserted into auth_http request headers and the XCLIENT command sent to the backend SMTP server, allowing injection.
notes: Affected 0.6.27-1.29.6; fixed in 1.29.7 and 1.28.3. The fix adds ngx_mail_smtp_validate_host(), allowing only RFC 1034 host name characters. The places that use the name (auth_http request, XCLIENT) are named in CHANGES and the commit message; their functions were not read.

classes: Whether declared controls actually take effect
Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: When client certificate OCSP validation was added to the stream module, ngx_stream_ssl_handler() checked the certificate verification result but not the OCSP status (ngx_ssl_ocsp_get_status()) that the http module checks, so a connection whose client certificate OCSP rejected was accepted even with ssl_ocsp configured.
notes: Affected 1.27.2-1.29.6; fixed in 1.29.7 and 1.28.3. Regression from 581cf22 (https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/581cf22673fc63e206693294161ea32e691a432f), which added ssl_ocsp to the stream module. Needs ssl_verify_client with ssl_ocsp in a stream server.

root_cause: SSL on upstream connections starts only in the write event handler, but when read and write events fired in the same event loop iteration the read handler ran first and ngx_http_upstream_process_header() parsed data that arrived before the SSL handshake as the upstream response.
notes: Affected 1.3.0-1.29.4; fixed in 1.29.5 and 1.28.2. Affects SSL-enabled upstream connections only. The fix makes the header processing detect data read before the handshake and fail over to the next upstream.

root_cause: ngx_mail_auth_plain(), ngx_mail_auth_login_username(), ngx_mail_auth_login_password() and ngx_mail_auth_cram_md5() wrote the session login or password data pointer before base64 decoding succeeded, so a decoding error left new data with the old length, and a later read with that length went out of bounds.
notes: Affected 0.7.22-1.29.0; fixed in 1.29.1. The advisory names ngx_mail_smtp_module as where the over-read shows up; the code that later reads the stale length was not located in the patch. The CVE-to-commit mapping follows the matching commit date (2025-08-12) and content.

root_cause: With TLSv1.3, OpenSSL resumes sessions in the default SSL context before the SNI callback runs, and ngx_http_ssl_servername() and ngx_stream_ssl_servername() did not check that a resumed session was established for the server name now selected, so a session from one virtual server was accepted on another that requires client certificate verification.
notes: Affected 1.11.4-1.27.3; fixed in 1.27.4 and 1.26.3. Needs several virtual servers on one listener, some with client certificate verification. The fix commit says an earlier restriction (b720f650b) covered only older protocol versions. Per the 0373fe5 commit message, the later switch to the ClientHello callback (1.29.2) supersedes and reverts this fix; use the refs listed here for the test.

root_cause: ngx_http_mp4_crop_stsc_data() computed (next_chunk - chunk) * samples in 32-bit arithmetic and did not check that stsc chunk numbers increase, so the product could overflow and the difference could wrap, producing invalid sample and chunk values that later made the stsz and stco update code read outside the atom buffers.
notes: Affected 1.5.13-1.27.0; fixed in 1.27.1 and 1.26.2. Fix spans two commits (7362d01: 64-bit multiplication; 88955b1: reject unordered chunks), together matching patch.2024.mp4.txt.

root_cause: ngx_http_v3_set_capacity() sized the QPACK dynamic table entry array for exactly the maximum entry count derived from the capacity, but an insert adds the new entry before evicting old ones, so when the table was full one entry was written past the end of the array.
notes: Affected 1.25.0-1.25.5 and 1.26.0; fixed in 1.27.0 and 1.26.1. The commit says the bug was introduced by 987bee4363d1. The insert routine that adds before evicting is in the same file; its name was not read. The advisory has no patch links; the mapping follows its title 'Buffer overwrite in HTTP/3'. The record cites the CISPA paper arXiv 2409.01059.

classes: Assumptions broken by callbacks and reentrancy
root_cause: The HTTP/3 decoder stream was created on demand, so sending a Stream Cancellation (ngx_http_v3_send_cancel_stream()) while a request stream was being drained created it through ngx_get_connection(), which drains connections and closed the same request stream again, recursing until the stack ran out or leaving a freed connection referenced up the stack.
notes: Affected 1.25.0-1.25.5 and 1.26.0; fixed in 1.27.0 and 1.26.1. The fix pre-creates the decoder stream in ngx_http_v3_init() when the dynamic table capacity is not zero. ngx_get_connection() and ngx_drain_connections() are core functions named in the commit message. The advisory has no patch links; the mapping follows its title 'Stack overflow and use-after-free in HTTP/3', which matches the commit message.

root_cause: For a zero-length literal field line, ngx_http_v3_parse_field_lri(), ngx_http_v3_parse_field_l() and ngx_http_v3_parse_field_lpbi() took a shortcut branch that never set st->value.data, so a NULL data pointer was passed to the header handlers.
notes: Affected 1.25.0-1.25.5 and 1.26.0; fixed in 1.27.0 and 1.26.1. The advisory has no patch links; the mapping follows its title 'NULL pointer dereference in HTTP/3'.

root_cause: ngx_quic_handle_crypto_frame() did not ignore CRYPTO frames for a packet level whose keys had already been discarded after handshake completion (for example frames sent in the same packet as the client Finished), and ngx_quic_free_buffer() left last_chain pointing at freed chains, so later processing used released buffers.
notes: Affected 1.25.0-1.25.5 and 1.26.0; fixed in 1.27.0 and 1.26.1. The advisory says memory disclosure only on systems with MTU larger than 4096 bytes. The CVE-to-commit mapping is inferred (the advisory has no patch links): 6f8c520 says it prevents memory disclosure, 9ddc6a0 is use-after-free hardening released at the same time.

root_cause: On a key phase change, ngx_quic_decrypt() used the next-key crypto context without checking that it existed, so a packet with a flipped key phase while next keys were missing dereferenced a NULL context; the fix uses next keys only when present and otherwise tries the current keys.
notes: Affected 1.25.3 only; fixed in 1.25.4. The CVE-to-commit mapping is inferred: the advisory has no patch links, the commit cites trac #2585 (segfault on missing next keys), and third-party databases give the same mapping. The record says the context could be NULL after an earlier context reuse change; that change was not identified.

root_cause: When ngx_quic_shutdown_stream() failed in ngx_quic_stream_cleanup_handler(), the error branch returned without clearing qs->connection, so the QUIC stream kept a pointer to the stream connection already freed by the application, and a later close freed it a second time.
notes: Affected 1.25.0-1.25.3; fixed in 1.25.4. The CVE-to-commit mapping is inferred: the advisory has no patch links, the commit cites trac #2586 (double free on stream cleanup), and third-party databases give the same mapping.

root_cause: The mp4 atom readers did not reject atoms that may appear only once in their container, so a duplicate atom overwrote only part of the saved buffers and counts, leaving data and sizes from different atom instances and leading to memory corruption.
notes: Affected 1.1.3-1.23.1 and 1.0.7-1.0.15; fixed in 1.23.2 and 1.22.1. Same fix as CVE-2022-41742 (one commit, matching patch.2022.mp4.txt, adds duplicate checks to 21 atom readers). The exact path from duplicate atom to memory corruption is inferred in the record.

root_cause: The mp4 atom readers did not reject atoms that may appear only once in their container, so a duplicate atom overwrote only part of the saved buffers and counts, leaving data and sizes from different atom instances, which shows up as worker memory disclosure.
notes: Affected 1.1.3-1.23.1 and 1.0.7-1.0.15; fixed in 1.23.2 and 1.22.1. Same commit and root cause as CVE-2022-41741; a blind audit run for one covers both.

root_cause: ngx_resolver_copy() sized a DNS name in one pass and copied it in a second pass that appended a '.' after a label whenever the next length byte was nonzero, including when that byte was a compression pointer after the last label, so the copy wrote one byte more than the sizing pass counted.
notes: Affected 0.6.18-1.20.0; fixed in 1.21.0 and 1.20.1. Reached only when the resolver directive is configured. The GitHub commit makes the same change as patch.2021.resolver.txt (the '.' is now written before each label except the first).
